gist: A third of young British adults have never had sex, according to a major study.
Adults in Great Britain are having sex less frequently than in past decades.
Online sexual activities like sexting and watching pornography have become widespread among young people.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles found British adults are having less sex. Under-45s average sex twice a month, down from four times in 1990. A third of under-25s have never had sex, up from under a fifth in 2010. Meanwhile, half of 16- to 24-year-olds have sent or received sexual images in the past year.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Fewer young women want children, with the proportion doubling to 17% over the past decade. Researchers cite potential factors like economic insecurity, mental health issues, less physical socialising, and living with parents longer. Furthermore, many people still engage in unprotected sex, putting them at risk of sexually transmitted infections and unplanned pregnancies.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Researchers plan to investigate what is driving changing family plans and potential future impacts of AI companions on sexual behaviour. Public health services may also need to adapt to ensure equitable HPV vaccination coverage across all groups.

The survey fieldwork took place between September 2022 and January 2024.
The survey covered people across Great Britain.

sections.text: The disaster highlights the dangers of Indonesia's widespread illegal gold mining industry. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Model and artist Veruschka, born Vera von Lehndorff, has died at the age of 87. Born in 1939, she endured a traumatic childhood after her father was executed in 1944 for plotting to assassinate Adolf Hitler. She subsequently rose to fame in the 1960s as one of fashion's original supermodels.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Veruschka expanded the boundaries of fashion and beauty through body-transforming art and major collaborations with designers and photographers. Outlets differ slightly on her cover record: the BBC reports 13 American Vogue covers, whereas The Guardian notes hundreds of covers overall. She also starred in films including Blow Up and Casino Royale.

'Big moment' as net migration now in tens of thousands

gist: UK net migration has fallen to 77,000 in the year to June.
The drop is driven by fewer arrivals for work, study, and asylum.
Politicians from different parties dispute who deserves credit for the decrease.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: UK net migration fell to 77,000 in the year to June, down from 204,000 in the previous 12 months and a peak of 944,000 in 2023. This marks the lowest level since 1997 excluding the Covid pandemic. The decline was driven by drops in work visas, student arrivals, and asylum claims, following visa restrictions introduced by successive Conservative and Labour administrations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The figures fulfill a long-standing target to bring net migration into the tens of thousands, first pledged by David Cameron in 2010. While politicians welcomed the drop, researchers warned that falls in skilled work visas could carry a fiscal cost, while reductions in asylum migration may benefit public finances.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Researchers suggest net migration may drop further next year. Meanwhile, political debate continues, with the Conservatives calling for a legally binding annual cap and Labour defending its current policies.

gist: Extreme global heat caused unprecedented declines in global freshwater levels during 2023 and 2024.
Global river flows fell to 5.7% below normal while lake and reservoir storage dropped.
South America experienced particularly large decreases in river flows and surface water.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An international study led by the Chinese Academy of Sciences found that surface freshwater fell sharply across the world in 2023 and 2024. Global river flows dropped by about 5.7% below normal, and water stored in lakes and reservoirs decreased by 9.5%.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The findings highlight that a warmer atmosphere does not mean more available water on land, as additional rainfall often occurs over oceans. The study shows how exposed global water supplies are to climate change and extreme weather.

fivew: An international study led by the Chinese Academy of Sciences

quotes.text: The findings highlight an important paradox of climate change: a warmer atmosphere does not necessarily mean more water is available on land.

A former Metropolitan Police officer provided misleading evidence leading to Kololo's conviction.
Kololo's conviction was quashed, and he is now suing the Met for compensation.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In 2011, Somali gunmen killed David Tebbutt and abducted his wife Judith in Kenya. Kenyan police arrested Ali Kololo, a woodcutter, and tortured him into signing a statement. Metropolitan Police officers assisted the investigation. Former Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd presented misleading evidence and relied on Kololo's coerced statement, leading to Kololo's wrongful conviction for kidnap and robbery.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Kololo spent over ten years in prison, including three years on death row, before Kenya's High Court quashed his conviction in 2023. The Independent Office for Police Conduct found Hibberd had omitted forensic evidence. The wrongful imprisonment destroyed Kololo's health, marriage and family life, leaving him unable to work or support his children.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kololo is suing London's Metropolitan Police for compensation to rebuild his life and support his children. The Metropolitan Police force is contesting the legal claim, which lawyers say could take years to resolve.

sections.text: Eleven UN experts expressed alarm over the alleged abduction and detention of three pro-democracy activists: Tran Hiep, Nguyen Duc Thuan, and Thai Cong Truong Son. timeline.text: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants

gist: Canada's Supreme Court has largely upheld Quebec's ban on public servants wearing religious symbols.
The court confirmed Quebec could use the notwithstanding clause to shield Bill 21.
Critics called the ruling discriminatory, while Quebec leaders celebrated the protection of secularism.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Canada's Supreme Court largely upheld Quebec's Bill 21, which bans public sector workers from wearing religious symbols. It ruled Quebec could pre-emptively invoke the notwithstanding clause to shield the law, though it found the law infringes on democratic rights regarding elected officials with face coverings.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The decision highlights tensions between minority rights and government powers to override them. Critics argue the law excludes religious minorities, especially Muslim women, from public employment. Quebec contends it protects state secularism. While the law stands, courts retain the ability to declare charter infringements.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Prime Minister Mark Carney said his government will study the ruling's implications, while the Bloc Québécois pledged to continue preserving Quebec's distinct values.

timeline.text: ‘Genuinely emotional’: the world-conquering Chicken Shop Date’s final, eye-opening episode
Chicken Shop Date: The perfect end or a disappointing send-off?

gist: Amelia Dimoldenberg has ended her YouTube interview series Chicken Shop Date after over ten years.
The final episode featured psychotherapist Esther Perel instead of expected celebrity guests.
Dimoldenberg plans to focus on writing, including a romantic comedy, after ending the show.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Amelia Dimoldenberg concluded her YouTube series Chicken Shop Date after more than ten years. The final episode featured Belgian psychotherapist Esther Perel and played out like a therapy session. Some fans expected a bigger celebrity guest like Drake, but most viewers reacted positively. The final series was also screened in cinemas before the YouTube finale.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Starting as a youth club project, the show grew into a major stop on celebrity press tours, featuring stars such as Cher and Sir Paul McCartney. It influenced the interview landscape and helped shift online video into mainstream entertainment. However, early fans felt celebrity involvement reduced its initial charm, and Dimoldenberg noted feeling sad and exhausted by continuing.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Dimoldenberg wants to focus on writing in the future, including a romantic comedy, and aims to become a movie director. The Dimz Inc Academy, launched in 2025, will continue mentoring young people from underrepresented backgrounds.

gist: Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed for 14 and a half years for online blackmail.
He coerced girls globally into self-harm and animal abuse for an online network.
Police and charities warned of growing risks posed to children by Com networks.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Newcastle Crown Court sentenced 20-year-old Beau-Jack Mensforth to 14 and a half years in detention with an extended licence. Mensforth admitted 17 offences after coercing vulnerable girls across the UK, USA and Australia into self-harm, sharing sexual images and hurting animals for an online group called the Com.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Law enforcement and safety charities warn that Com networks pose an urgent threat to children worldwide. The UK National Crime Agency reported that Com activity rose sixfold between 2022 and 2024, with members using extortion, doxing and swatting for status, control and gratification.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Police urge parents to talk to their children and monitor their devices. Additionally, the Molly Rose Foundation safety charity has urged tech firms, regulators and international authorities to mount a joined-up response against the danger.

Mensforth was jailed on a Friday for criminal offences committed between 2023 and 2024.
The court proceedings took place at Newcastle Crown Court in north-east England.
Mensforth committed the abuses for content, notoriety, and to climb the hierarchy of an online harm group.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Jason Zadrozny was convicted of fraud and tax evasion after setting up a fake heritage society to scam a local authority. He transferred council funds into his own account and failed to pay tax on rental properties. He was subsequently sentenced to 27 months in prison and later resigned as a councillor.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The offences caused ten councillors to quit and led to government intervention. Officials launched a rapid review of the council after concerns were raised regarding his appointment to a planning committee following his conviction.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: A best-value assessment is being conducted into the local authority to ensure it meets required standards. There will be no by-election for his former seat until local elections take place in May.

timeline.text: New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking

gist: Satellite data reveals major African coastal cities are sinking faster than previously estimated.
Subsidence substantially increases flood exposure for millions of residents and billions in assets.
Human activities such as groundwater extraction and land reclamation drive much of the subsidence.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Virginia Tech researchers used Sentinel-1 satellite radar data to track land movement in 20 African coastal cities. They found cities including Lagos, Alexandria and Luanda are sinking faster than estimated by the IPCC in 2021. Alexandria and Lagos are sinking by an average of 6mm and 5mm per year respectively, while Durban has remained stable.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Subsidence lowers land relative to the sea, compounding climate-driven sea level rises. Alexandria faces sea level rises 36% higher by 2050 than previously projected. Seven million people and $180bn of assets could be at flood risk. Groundwater extraction, land reclamation and sediment trapping by the Aswan Dam contribute to the sinking.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Researchers suggest the satellite monitoring technique could be applied to regions like the Pacific islands. Better data may help African planners allocate resources, establish local policies to manage water extraction, supply alternative water sources, and construct flood defences.

fivew: Researchers from Virginia Tech, including Oluwaseyi Dasho and Manoochehr Shirzaei.

Subsidence is driven by natural factors alongside human activities such as groundwater extraction and land reclamation.

timeline.text: Schools in England must set aside time for pupils to read for pleasure
Set time aside for children to read for pleasure, schools to be told

gist: Schools in England must allocate regular time for pupils to read for pleasure.
Year 8 pupils will undergo mandatory reading checks under proposed national curriculum reforms.
The measures aim to address declining literacy rates and tackle rising screen time.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell is set to announce national curriculum reforms requiring schools in England to allocate dedicated time for pupils to read for pleasure. Primary schools must set aside time daily. Outlets disagree on secondary schools: the BBC reports time will be set aside weekly, whereas The Guardian states several days a week. Year 8 pupils will also take a compulsory reading test.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The government aims to tackle declining literacy rates and compete with screen time, particularly among disadvantaged children and boys. Research shows reading enjoyment in the UK has dropped to a two-decade low.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Powell will unveil the plans in Parliament on Monday. The government aims to halve the reading disadvantage gap by 2035, ensuring 80% of students meet expected reading standards. GCSE courses such as history and geography may also be slimmed down.

timeline.text: A clinic is reassessing people with ADHD and autism diagnoses - but critics fear it could deepen stigma

gist: A Swedish clinic offers ADHD and autism diagnosis reassessments for young adults.
Patients want reassessments because past diagnoses blocked them from certain careers.
Critics warn the clinic deepens stigma and treats neurodivergence as undesirable.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A government-funded clinic in Sweden called Mottagning Neuropsykiatri opened to reassess ADHD and autism diagnoses. Hundreds of people, including young adults barred from certain jobs, approached the clinic. Doctors evaluate current symptoms rather than past history and update medical records if patients no longer meet diagnostic criteria.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Critics and neurodiversity advocates fear the service reinforces the idea that neurodivergence is undesirable, deepens stigma, and pressures individuals who mask their symptoms to lose diagnoses. Some argue the focus should be on changing unfair employment restrictions instead of adapting individuals to society.

fivew: A psychiatric clinic opened to reassess ADHD and autism diagnoses.
Over recent decades and continuing currently.
Patients sought to remove barriers to careers, while critics warned against deepening stigma.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Vithabai Narayangaonkar led a celebrated career as a Tamasha singer and dancer in Maharashtra, performing through pregnancy and war. Despite her fame, financial mismanagement left her in debt, forcing her to disband her troupe in 1990. She died in 2002. Now, her life has inspired a Bollywood musical called Eetha.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Vithabai was an outspoken artist who addressed caste discrimination and poverty among Tamasha performers. While supporters celebrate her enduring legacy, critics have raised concerns that the new biographical film omits references to her caste and social struggle in her name.

fivew: Folk artist Vithabai Narayangaonkar and filmmaker Laxman Utekar.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cricket Australia broadened its independent inquiry regarding ball-tampering to also examine the Ashes series played in 2017-18. This followed claims made in a book by a former player suggesting the whole team knew about the tampering during a tour to South Africa. While some former team members supported these claims, current and other past players denied them.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The renewed focus brings fresh attention to a major past cricket scandal. The governing body stated that the inquiry provides a safe environment for participants to share accounts, while ensuring no retroactive punishments will occur.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The independent forum will remain open for six weeks, inviting past players, support staff, and management to contribute. A full report containing recommendations will be published within thirty days after the board receives it.

timeline.text: Twickenham set to be half empty for Nations Championship finals opening night

gist: Twickenham is set to be about half empty for the opening night of the finals.
Ticket sales are stronger for the Saturday and Sunday matches of the weekend.
Organisers faced tight deadlines, diary and budget constraints, and stadium size challenges.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Nations Championship finals opening night at Allianz Stadium is set to be filled to about half its capacity. The uppermost tier is closed, and only a portion of the middle and lower tiers are open for the Italy versus Fiji and Ireland versus Australia matches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The low attendance highlights challenges in marketing a new tournament format with late team confirmations, alongside high stadium capacity and pre-Christmas budget constraints.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Organisers will conduct a debrief before cities can bid to host the next tournament in 2028, with potential changes including using multiple smaller venues.

timeline.text: Decline of deities - the long game the All Blacks cannot afford to lose

gist: The All Blacks face a rare decline in form and financial stability.
Financial struggles threaten New Zealand Rugby's ability to keep top players at home.
Growing departures of mid-career stars and reliance on tradition present ongoing challenges.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The All Blacks have suffered a downturn, on course for their least successful decade since the 1970s and facing a potential sixth defeat of the calendar year. Financially, New Zealand Rugby faces projected multi-million-pound losses, leading to the departure of star players to overseas clubs in France and Japan.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Financial pressures and the loss of mid-career talent threaten the team's global dominance and historic legacy. While traditional coaching methods and domestic eligibility rules once protected the All Blacks, rising costs and competitive overseas salaries make it harder to retain top players.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The All Blacks prepare to play England at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham aiming to avoid another defeat as New Zealand Rugby navigates a challenging long-term financial and strategic future.

timeline.text: Five-try Ireland beat Australia in autumn finale

gist: Ireland beat Australia 38-14 in their autumn finale in London.
Ireland secured fifth place in the inaugural Nations Championship.
James McNabney scored two late tries for Ireland.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ireland defeated Australia 38-14 in London to finish the year with four consecutive autumn wins. Australia took an early lead through a try by Jeremy Williams. Ireland replied with 24 unanswered points, including tries from Robbie Henshaw, Nick Timoney and Robert Baloucoune. Kalani Thomas scored for Australia, before replacement James McNabney added two late tries.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory secured a fifth-place finish for Ireland in the inaugural Nations Championship. Ireland finished the year with 10 wins from 12 internationals.
